subject: Scheduling: throughput & latency benchmarking briefing with Acme
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Leah Wong <leah.w@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Scheduling: throughput & latency benchmarking briefing with Acme

Hi Sam / Leah —

Thanks again for the productive discovery call last week. Per our conversation, we'd like to run a short technical briefing (30–45m) to align on the upcoming performance benchmark goals and agree on the load-test plan and success criteria. Proposed objectives:

- Review target SLAs and throughput goals (sustained tokens/sec, peak tails)
- Walk through Redwood's planned load generator config and dataset slices
- Confirm KV/prefix-caching expectations and 95/99 latency targets
- Agree on run owners, data access, and next steps (preflight runs, production-like test window)

Proposed slots (PST / Acme local times):
- Tue Jan 19, 10:00–10:45 PT (1:00–1:45 ET)
- Tue Jan 19, 14:00–14:45 PT (5:00–5:45 ET)
- Wed Jan 20, 09:00–09:45 PT (12:00–12:45 ET)

Required attendees: engineering lead (Acme), performance owner (Redwood: Marissa), infra lead (Redwood: Karthik).

Background/targets to consider before the meeting: our initial ask is to validate that the dedicated config can sustain ~8k tokens/sec with 95th pct latency under 150ms at 2048-token window for your observed prompt mix. We'll bring a readout of previous microbenchmarks and a draft run plan (attached).

Attachments: load_test_plan_v2.pdf (draft), meeting_notes_template.docx

If none of these slots work, please propose 2 alternatives and we'll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Wong <leah.w@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Scheduling: throughput & latency benchmarking briefing with Acme

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the fast follow. We want to be part of this and the agenda looks good. Quick schedule note: our infra lead (Leah) is out Tue afternoon and we have an org-wide all-hands Wed 12–2 ET which blocks the 14:00 PT slot.

Can we do Tue Jan 19 at 10:00 PT or Wed Jan 20 at 09:00 PT? If neither works we can do Thu morning.

Also, curious — when you say 8k tokens/sec, is that sustained RPS across a single model instance or across the pool? Helpful to clarify so we can align internal capacity checks beforehand.

Best,
Sam
Sam Patel
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Corp
sam.patel@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scheduling: throughput & latency benchmarking briefing with Acme

Hi Sam —

10:00 PT on Tue (Jan 19) works for the Redwood perf team — I'll lead the briefing. To Sam's question: our target phrasing was across the Dedicated pool we'll provision for Acme (not one single process). In the briefing we'll show both single-instance microbenchmarks and pool-level sustained throughput curves, plus guidance on headroom.

Can you and Leah attach any representative prompt mixes or run constraints (max tokens, typical streaming vs. non-streaming ratio) before the meeting? That'll let us tailor the load pattern (burstiness, seq-length distribution).

I've attached the current load test config (load_test_config.yaml) and a small KV metrics snapshot (kv_metrics_snapshot.csv) that we plan to use in the readout. If you want, Ben can run a quick preflight tomorrow evening to sanity-check the harness against your sample prompts.

Attachments: load_test_config.yaml, kv_metrics_snapshot.csv

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 07:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scheduling: throughput & latency benchmarking briefing with Acme

Quick note from the infra side before the meeting:

- We'll need a shadow dataset (anonymized) of ~1k prompts to run realistic seq-length distributions. If Acme can't share, we'll synthesize a distribution from the sample stats.
- Preflight plan: run a 10-min sanity run at 20% scale and a 1-hr sustained run at 50% scale before the full test window. Ben, please confirm availability to run the preflight Tue 19 18:00 PT.
- Runbook / parameters: TARGET_SUSTAINED_TOK_SEC=8000; PEAK_BURST_MULTIPLIER=2.5; SEQ_DISTRIBUTION_FILE=drive:/abc123/prompt_dist.json

I'm linking the runbook and the Jira ticket here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/abc123-loadtests and Jira: PERF-482. We should flag any SLO relaxation required for prefix-heavy workloads.

Ben, can you confirm you'll take the preflight run and share logs to the shared folder?

Thanks — Karthik
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Leah Wong <leah.w@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Confirmed: Tue Jan 19 10:00 PT perf briefing (calendar invite)

Thanks all — scheduling confirmed for Tue Jan 19, 10:00–10:45 PT. I've sent a calendar invite with the hangouts link and added the shared drive folder to the invite. Quick checklist for tomorrow's briefing:

- Acme: attach representative prompt set or confirm we can use synthesized distribution (Leah / Sam)
- Redwood: Marissa to present load_test_plan_v2.pdf and Ben to share preflight logs if available
- Both: review target definition (TARGET_SUSTAINED_TOK_SEC=8000; 95th < 150ms at 2048 tokens) and confirm any relaxations
- Ops: confirm whether test window requires specific IP allowlist or VPC peering prep (if so, we'll get the security ticket opened)

Attachments included in invite: load_test_plan_v2.pdf, meeting_notes_template.docx

If anything changes, reply inline and we'll update the invite. Looking forward to the session.

Cheers,
Hannah
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
